chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): A man urinates while he is in a state of major ritual impurity (junub), then he cleans his private part (istinja), and his garment touches his body while he is still wet. He (peace be upon him) said: There is no problem.

key_terms.جُنُبٌ: A person in a state of major ritual impurity requiring full body wash (ghusl)
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem / It is permissible
key_terms.يَسْتَنْجِي: To clean the private parts after urination or defecation

ai.seo_question: Is a garment considered impure if it touches the wet body of someone who is still in a state of major ritual impurity (junub) after urinating?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the principle of *al-istishab* (presumption of continuity of purity) for garments, ruling that minor contact with a *junub*'s sweat or urine does not render the clothing impure (*najis*). This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it alleviates the burden of ritual purity, distinguishing between major impurity (*junub*) and the physical substance of urine/sweat itself.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Muawiya Bin Ammar who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The man urinates and he is with sexual impurity. Then he cleans his private part, and his clothes hit his body and he is wet’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yunus from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who urinates while he has experienced sexual relation. He then cleanses himself and his clothes touch his body while it is wet. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not harmful.’”
